title: SLO-aware commit bucketizer and buffer model
body:
Purpose:
This sheet is a working simulation and recommendation draft for pricing/reservation design that is explicitly SLO-aware (latency P95 targets) and uses a bucketized commit model plus a small elastic buffer credit to reduce waste from short-term spikes. It is intended to be a pragmatic complement to the existing reserve/capacity docs with these differentiators:
- Buckets map commits to SLO tiers (low-latency, standard, background) rather than only to GPU counts or dollar tiers.
- We introduce a short-horizon "buffer credit" (hours of burstable capacity) that amortizes across customers to limit overcommit risk.
- Cost allocation separates amortized idle, burst, and maintenance in the effective unit price.

Top-line definitions and formulas (one-line spreadsheet-friendly):
- Committed_GPUs = integer commit by customer (v100-equivalent units).
- Baseline_Throughput = Committed_GPUs * Nominal_GPU_TokensPerHour.
- Average_Utilization = ObservedTokens/ Baseline_Throughput (can exceed 1 due to autoscaling/burst).
- Buffer_Capacity_hours = CustomerBufferHours * Committed_GPUs.
- Burst_Charge = max(0, Burst_Hours - Buffer_Capacity_hours) * OnDemandRatePerGPUHour.
- Amortized_Idle = max(0, (Committed_GPUs - EquivalentAvgActiveGPUs)) * ReservedRatePerGPUHour.
- Effective_Unit_Cost = (CommittedCost + Burst_Charge + Amortized_IdleAllocation + MaintenanceAllocation) / EffectiveTokenCount

Key assumptions (editable cells):
- Nominal_GPU_TokensPerHour = 120k tokens (p99 model mix).
- ReservedRatePerGPUHour = $2.40 (example; adjust per region/hardware).
- OnDemandRatePerGPUHour = $4.80.
- CustomerBufferHours default = 6 hours per 8-GPU commit slab (scaled linearly).
- MaintenanceAllocation = 5% of reserved monthly cost (network, storage, software).
- BillingWindow = monthly calendar.

Bucketization logic (sample):
- SLO-LowLatency bucket: commits targeted for <150ms P95, requires pinned pools / lower packing. Pricing: base discount = 12% from list, lower buffer share, higher reserved overhead.
- SLO-Standard bucket: <300ms P95, aggressive batching allowed; pricing: base discount = 26%.
- SLO-Background bucket: best-effort, used for embeddings/async workloads; pricing: base discount = 42%, larger preemptable mix allowed.

Illustrative mini-table (column headers; rows are scenario samples):
Scenario,Committed_GPUs,Avg_Util%,Peak_to_Avg_ratio,Buffer_Hours,OnDemand_Burst_Hours,Burst_Charge,Amortized_Idle,Effective_Unit_Cost
Conservative-Std,16,0.72,1.9,96,18,$86,$420,$0.00068
Aggressive-Mix,32,0.89,2.6,192,40,$192,$360,$0.00052

Notes on the mini-table: Burst_Charge and Amortized_Idle are sample outputs using the formulas above with a 30-day month. Effective_Unit_Cost is tokens-based (per token) for pricing guidance to compare to hosted per-token list.

Why bucket + buffer reduces waste:
1) Bucketing by SLO lets us reduce packing inefficiency for latency-sensitive commits while channeling best-effort workloads into high-utilization pools.
2) A small shared buffer (hours scaled with commit size) mutes tail spikes (e.g., short marketing bursts or load tests) so customers don't need to over-commit for rare events.
3) Buffer usage is charged as a separate line-item with clear accounting to avoid hidden cross-subsidies.

Sensitivity knobs included in the sheet (cells to iterate):
- BufferHoursPerGPU: 0–24 (linear scaling)
- PreemptableMix: 0–80% (affects reserved vs spot effective rate)
- PoolFragilitySurcharge: 0–20% (for small customer pools that fragment utilization)
- SLO-Premium multiplier: 1.0–1.3 applied to reserved rate for low-latency buckets
- BurstCapPolicy: immediate-on-demand vs queued-burst (affects observed burst hours)

Sample recommendations (initial):
- Pilot a three-bucket product with the following defaults: LowLatency = 10% buffer, Standard = 20% buffer, Background = 40% buffer (buffer expressed as buffer-hours per GPU normalized to commit size).
- Price each bucket with a clear breakdown line items: base reserved charge, buffer allowance credit, measured burst overage, preemptable discount component.
- Add an automated utilization report that shows: rolling 7-day utilization, buffer draw (hours used), and projected next-month breakeven delta vs on-demand. That should be surfaced in Console as an "Efficiency" card.
- For customers with peak_to_avg_ratio > 3x, recommend a short-term partnership: 3-month reduced committed ramp + larger buffer for initial 30 days while workload patterns stabilize.

Open questions / to validate in next experiments:
- Optimal buffer sizing function: linear with commit vs diminishing returns? (Experiment with f(x)=k*x and f(x)=k*sqrt(x)).
- Behavioral response: will customers game buffer usage (e.g., schedule load tests during buffer windows)? Consider policy windows and enforcement.
- Hardware mix impact: accounting for A100 vs T4 costs changes Effective_Unit_Cost—need per-hardware templates.

Next steps and owners:
- Experiment implementation (ENG, Miguel) — instrument a month of reserved pools with buffer tracking; flag usage at customer-level (JIRA-DED-3121).
- Pricing drafts (PRODUCT, Priya) — produce a one-page external-facing pricing summary and an internal rate card that maps bucket to baseline hourly rate + sample monthly invoice (due 2024-12-15).
- Console telemetry (DX, Lena) — add Efficiency card hooks (signals: buffer_used_hours, reserved_util, burst_hours) and a sample UI mock (due 2025-01-20).
- Legal / Billing ops (Finance, Samir) — validate invoice line items and accounting treatment for amortized idle and buffer credits.

Appendix: quick cell formulas to paste into a sheet (A1-style references are placeholders):
- C2 = B2 * Nominal_GPU_TokensPerHour  // Baseline throughput
- D2 = ObservedTokens / C2  // Avg utilization
- E2 = CustomerBufferHours * B2  // Buffer capacity in hours*GPU
- F2 = max(0, ObservedBurstHours - E2) * OnDemandRatePerGPUHour  // Burst charge
- G2 = max(0, (B2 - EquivalentAvgActiveGPUs)) * ReservedRatePerGPUHour * HoursInMonth  // Amortized idle
- H2 = (ReservedMonthlyCost + F2 + Maintenance) / EffectiveTokenCount  // Effective unit cost

Unresolved metrics to collect (for better calibration):
- Per-customer short-term spike distribution (empirical PDF of burst durations).
- Correlation between SLO tier and observed packing inefficiency.
- Realistic on-demand charge elasticity when customers see explicit burst invoices.

If this approach looks promising, I suggest we run a 4-week pilot with 12 mid-market customers who have demonstrated multi-modal demand (embedding + real-time chat), instrument buffer telemetry, and test three buffer-sizing functions (linear, sqrt, plateau). Output should be a summary spreadsheet with delta to committed spend and customer satisfaction change (NPS micro-survey after a buffer-trigger event).

Comments / notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light on final numbers; we need region/hardware-specific rates. Use the linked pricing-sim PR for a runnable baseline.
- I expect the final external product to show a simple three-line invoice per month (reserved baseline, buffer used, burst overage) and an "efficiency" dashboard targeting engineers.
